policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the interrogative clause 'seest thou what they do?', which requires the qere מָה הֵם ('what they [are doing]'). The ketiv מהם is the prepositional 'from them' and leaves the ASV's 'what they do' without a source. Both notes on this verse are classed alternative_rendering (English wording for the 'go far off' clause and for 'thou shalt again see'), so neither bears on the choice; the ASV wording alone decides it.
